title: A Simple, Nearly-Optimal Algorithm for Differentially Private All-Pairs Shortest Distances

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Introduction states Sealfon's bounded-edge-weight result for the (ε,δ)-DP setting is 'Õ(√(nM/ε))', i.e. scaling as n^{1/2}M^{1/2}ε^{-1/2}. However, Section 1.4 describes the same result as 'O(√n·M·log(1/δ)/ε·log(n·M·ε/γ))', i.e. scaling as n^{1/2}·M·ε^{-1} (M and ε appear with different exponents than in the Introduction's claim). These two statements about the identical cited result from [Sea16] are mathematically inconsistent (different polynomial dependence on M and ε), so at least one of them misrepresents the cited result.

Theorem 3.2 claims the (ε,δ)-DP error is O(n^{1/4}·log^2(n)·√log(2/δ)·log(1/γ)/ε). The proof derives error (5) as O(√s·log^{1.5}(n)·√log(2/δ)·log(2sn/γ)/ε) and error (2) as O(√(n/s)·log^{1.5}(n)·log(1/γ)/ε), and chooses s=√n/(log(n)·√log(2/δ)) to balance them. Substituting this s into either expression (after simplifying log(2sn/γ)=O(log(n)log(1/γ)) via Proposition E.2, which does not introduce extra δ-dependence since the δ-term sits in the denominator of s) yields a final bound scaling as n^{1/4}·log^2(n)·(log(2/δ))^{1/4}·log(1/γ)/ε — i.e. the δ-term should appear as (log(2/δ))^{1/4}, not √log(2/δ)=(log(2/δ))^{1/2} as stated. This is confirmed by checking that the analogous pure-DP derivation (Theorem 3.1, s=n^{1/3}/log^{2/3}(n)) correctly reproduces the stated log^{11/6}(n) factor, but performing the same careful substitution in the (ε,δ)-DP case produces a different (lower) power of log(2/δ) than claimed.

In the proof, each of the t·k trees is released via an ε/(t·k)-DP instantiation of Corollary 4.1 (with t:=⌈100·n^{1/k}log(n)⌉, so t·k = Θ(k·n^{1/k}·log n)). The resulting per-tree error should scale with the reciprocal of this privacy budget, i.e. as O(t·k·log^{1.5}(n)·log(n·t·k/γ)/ε) = O(k·n^{1/k}·log(n)·log^{1.5}(n)·log(n·t·k/γ)/ε). However, the paper writes this bound as 'O(k·n^{1/k}·log^{1.5}(n)·log(n·t·k/γ)/ε)', omitting the factor of log(n) contained in t. Carrying this dropped log(n) factor through the subsequent simplification (which converts log^{1.5}(n)·log(ntk/γ) into log^{2.5}(n)·log(k)·log(1/γ)) implies the correctly derived final bound should be O(k·n^{1/k}·log^{3.5}(n)·log(k)·log(1/γ)/ε), not the stated O(k·n^{1/k}·log^{2.5}(n)·log(k)·log(1/γ)/ε). The same issue propagates to Theorem 4.4, which uses the identical N=t·k construction.
